raw_case_text:
A 57-year-old man with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma presented to another institution 4 days after his third cycle of rituximab, cyclophosphamide, adriamycin, vincristine and prednisone (R-CHOP) with headache, malaise and fevers up to 102  F. A chest computerized tomography (CT) showed a right upper lobe opacity concerning for pneumonia. He received 11 days of empiric vancomycin, cefepime and doxycycline for tickborne diseases and was discharged home to complete an additional 7-day course of levofloxacin and doxycycline. He continued to feel unwell and was readmitted to our institution the following day with malaise and tachycardia. His past medical history was significant for follicular lymphoma, localized below the diaphragm with extra-nodal (lumbar spine) involvement diagnosed 4 months prior to presentation, hypertension and pulmonary embolism. He worked as a computer programmer and had not traveled outside of New England. He had no history of animal exposures. His vital signs on admission were: temperature 100.5  F, blood pressure 130/90 mm Hg, heart rate 130/min, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air; he was not in distress. He had no peripheral lymphadenopathy or skin lesions. His cardiovascular, pulmonary, abdominal and neurologic exams were unremarkable. His laboratory workup was notable for lymphopenia (absolute lymphocyte count of 250 cells/muL) and hyponatremia (125 mEq/L). Blood, urine and sputum cultures were negative. Positron emission tomography/CT (PET/CT) performed to evaluate for lymphoma progression showed enlarged, fluoro-2-deoxy-D-glucose (FDG)-avid mediastinal lymphadenopathy, which was new compared to 3 months prior, and had a maximum standardized uptake value (SUV) of 7, suggestive of active lymphoma (Fig. 1A). A bronchoscopy with ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration of a mediastinal lymph node was performed.
Hematoxylin-eosin (Fig. 1B) and mucicarmine (Fig. 1C) stains of an endobronchial ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspirate from the lymph node revealed many encapsulated yeast forms with narrow-based budding, morphologically consistent with Cryptococcus species, and no malignant cells. Serum cryptococcal antigen titer was 1:128. CD4+ lymphocyte count was 78 cells/muL and he was HIV negative. Although the headache that he initially presented with had resolved, a lumbar puncture was performed. The opening pressure was 28 mm Hg. The cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) white blood cell count was 365 cells/muL, 87% of which were neutrophils, and protein was elevated (416 mg/dL, normal range: 40 - 70 mg/dL). Cryptococcal antigen in the CSF was also positive (1:128), and CSF cultures grew Cryptococcus neoformans.
Our patient received induction treatment with liposomal amphotericin-B (5 mg/kg daily) and 5-flucytosine (100 mg/kg daily) for 2 weeks. His symptoms resolved, repeat CSF cultures were negative, and he transitioned to oral fluconazole 800 mg daily for 8 weeks, and 400 mg daily until completion of chemotherapy, with the plan to continue 200 mg of fluconazole daily (maintenance) indefinitely, at least until lymphocyte count recovery.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 57-year-old man with follicular non-Hodgkin's lymphoma presented with persistent malaise, headache, and fevers up to 102 F following his third cycle of R-CHOP chemotherapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Four days after completing his third cycle of R-CHOP chemotherapy, the patient presented to an outside hospital with headache, malaise, fevers up to 102 F, and a right upper lobe opacity on chest CT. Despite 11 days of inpatient vancomycin, cefepime, and doxycycline followed by discharge on oral levofloxacin and doxycycline, his malaise and tachycardia persisted, prompting readmission the next day.
subjective.past_medical_history: Subdiaphragmatic follicular non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with extranodal lumbar spine involvement (diagnosed 4 months prior, treated with 3 cycles of R-CHOP), hypertension, and pulmonary embolism. Computer programmer with no travel outside New England or animal exposures.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for malaise, prior headache, and fevers. Recent medications: R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone), vancomycin, cefepime, levofloxacin, and doxycycline.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vital signs: temperature 100.5 F, blood pressure 130/90 mmHg, heart rate 130 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, SpO2 98% on room air. No acute distress, no peripheral lymphadenopathy or skin lesions, and unremarkable cardiovascular, pulmonary, abdominal, and neurological examinations.
objective.routine_investigations: Lymphopenia (absolute lymphocyte count 250 cells/uL), hyponatremia (sodium 125 mEq/L), negative blood, urine, and sputum cultures, negative HIV test, and positive serum cryptococcal antigen titer of 1:128.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-lymphocyte count was 78 cells/uL. Outside chest CT showed a right upper lobe opacity; 18F-FDG PET/CT revealed new enlarged FDG-avid mediastinal lymphadenopathy (SUVmax 7). Endobronchial ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (EBUS-FNA) of a mediastinal lymph node showed numerous narrow-based budding encapsulated yeast forms on H&E and mucicarmine stains without malignant cells. Lumbar puncture revealed opening pressure 28 mmHg, CSF WBC 365 cells/uL (87% neutrophils), elevated protein 416 mg/dL (normal: 40-70 mg/dL), CSF cryptococcal antigen titer 1:128, and CSF culture growing Cryptococcus neoformans.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of disseminated Cryptococcus neoformans infection (mediastinal lymphadenitis mimicking FDG-avid lymphoma progression, pulmonary infiltrate, and cryptococcal meningitis) in an HIV-negative R-CHOP-treated follicular lymphoma patient, confirmed by EBUS-FNA mediastinal lymph node H&E and mucicarmine staining, serum and CSF CrAg titers of 1:128, and CSF culture isolating C. neoformans. Treated with 2 weeks of induction therapy using IV liposomal amphotericin B (5 mg/kg/day) and oral 5-flucytosine (100 mg/kg/day), achieving symptom resolution and CSF sterilization, followed by oral fluconazole consolidation (800 mg/day for 8 weeks, then 400 mg/day through chemotherapy completion) and planned indefinite maintenance (200 mg/day).
